title: As Jeremy Jordan as Floyd Collins once said “believe in what you can’...
transcript: I love when your plans derail and you have to pivot and you end up pivoting to a piece of theater that opens up a fascinating conversation around mysticism and religion that is exactly what happened when I went to go see Mystic Conversations at Theater Row I was originally at Theater Row to see the closing night of all the world’s A stage which unfortunately was sold out and I did not get off the waitlist but while I was waiting to see if I would get off the waitlist I got to meet the playwright of Mystic Conversations Julia Barry Bell in the lobby of Theater Row and hearing her describe this play was so intriguing to me it's about a mother who after meeting a woman at a hair salon who has a connection to the spiritual world finds out that her son may also have a connection to the spirits beyond our physical realm and this play opens up some really fascinating conversations around the spiritual realm and religion but also grief uh and especially grief when it comes to miscarriages which you don't often see in theater but in the midst of all of these deep philosophical conversations you also have this really charming relationship between a mother and her son as they both learn about each other and while there were parts of this play that I could definitely critique in terms of the writing the direction and the performances that weren't as strong as I usually see on a stage there is something about this story that kept me engaged the entire time I just was invested in it like in terms of the direction there were moments where I feel like performers could have been given a little more motivation as to what they were doing in the scene especially if they weren't really talking or if they were listening to other characters I felt like moments could take more time to settle and on the flip side of that they were aspects of this direction that I really loved like what they were trying to do with all of the transitions in setting up each of the new scenes and involving the actors in all set changes and even today a few days after seeing this play I'm still thinking of some of the topics brought up in the show which I think some of the best theater does it keeps you thinking about it even after you leave the theater and opens up you to new conversations Mystic conversations is an incredibly limited run only playing through May 17th at Theater Row there are discount tickets available including on TDF right now
